basis: A catalogue price that is a one-piece price (no break table, or a table that ends below 10 pcs). Factor = median ratio of the highest published break to the one-piece price over 73 LCSC listings of BOM parts with at least 4 breaks in prices.csv: 0.52 (quartiles 0.49-0.58; median highest break 6,000 pcs). TI.com 1ku / one-piece over 58 listings is 0.45 (quartiles 0.35-0.50): the LCSC figure is the more cautious. Computed 2026-10-04.

A priced line whose listing publishes breaks above 10 pcs but none at 1,000 pcs (e.g. a distributor table that ends at 100 or 504). Factor = median ratio of the highest LCSC break to the break at or below 1,000 pcs over the same 73 listings: 0.85 (quartiles 0.75-1.00).

An estimated purchased part (Chinese semiconductor, IC, film capacitor, connector, sensor) whose catalogue figure is a 500-1000 piece level taken from a sibling listing, a related RFQ or an engineering estimate: the same LCSC ratio, 0.85 (quartiles 0.75-1.00). A 5,000-module build buys 15,000-120,000 of such parts a year; no quote exists for any of them.

An estimated fuse, relay, contactor, surge protector or varistor: LCSC protection-group listings (13) give a median ratio highest break / break at 1,000 pcs of 0.77; rounded to 0.80. Western maker list prices (Mersen, ETI, Siemens, TDK) have no published breaks above 100 pcs; a quotation is needed.

Fallback for a GENERIC class price whose example listing is not in prices.csv: median ratio highest break / reel break (4,000-5,000 pcs) over 56 class examples in prices.csv = 0.96 (minimum 0.74). Normally the example listing itself is read (REAL).

Wound custom magnetics priced by material and labour (PV inductor rev M2 edgewise, 44.6 USD: POCO cores 16 + magnet wire 13.6 + insulation 4 = 33.6 of 40.5 before the 10 % margin = 83 % material; winding and test 7 = 17 %). At 15,000 inductors a year: material x 0.90 (assumed 10 % bulk discount on cores and copper), labour x 0.60 (semi-automatic toroid winder and test fixture): 0.83 x 0.90 + 0.17 x 0.60 = 0.85. Also applied to the port ring and the DAB magnetics of the old platform.

Small potted transformers: the magnetics designer's own 5,000-unit figures. 75 W auxiliary transformer 8.5 -> 5.7 USD (design_aux75_transformer.json build_5k_usd) = 0.67; gate-bias transformer 2.18 -> 1.22 USD plus 4,000 USD bobbin tooling over 15,000 parts (0.27 each) = 0.68.

Custom metal and moulded parts (DC terminals, busbars, extrusion heatsink with clips, shutters, guards, standoffs, probes, cold plate): raw copper/aluminium about 60 % of the price at 0.95 (annual metal contracts), conversion (die and stamping tooling amortised, fixtures, machining time) 40 % at 0.70: 0.60 x 0.95 + 0.40 x 0.70 = 0.85.
Cable harnesses: labour about 50 % of the price at 0.65 (cut-and-crimp machines, jigs), wire and connectors 50 % at 0.95: 0.80.
AlN insulators: sintered ceramics are priced by quantity and a 5,000-module build buys 120,000-160,000 pads a year; no quote. The architect's list assumed 0.60; 0.70 is used here.
Bare boards outside the BOM: fab price at 5,000 boards a year against about 1,000: panel utilisation and copper-clad volume; assumed 15 % (no quote).
Board assembly outside the BOM: 15 million placements a year instead of 3 million at a Chinese EMS house, and stencil, fixture and programming cost spread over 5,000 modules; assumed 20 % (no quote).
Sheet-metal chassis, covers and packaging: progressive-die tooling amortised over 5,000 sets; assumed 15 % (no quote).
Final assembly, test and burn-in: test-rack share and operator learning over 5,000 modules; assumed 15 % (no quote).
